children: Japan's Nikkei share average climbed as technology investor SoftBank Group rebounded from a selloff in the previous session, while traders reassessed calls by executives in U.S. artificial intelligence companies for a slowdown in AI development.
recouped early losses to rise roughly 1% to 64,082.36 by the midday break. The broader Topix
surged 9.13%, recouping part of the previous session's 10.7% loss after a selloff in AI-linked stocks sparked by warnings from industry leaders about the technology's risks.
"Japan was the first market that was hit by the warning from the AI leaders in the previous session," said Kazuaki Shimada, chief strategist at IwaiCosmo Securities.
"The morning after, investors thought it was too early to judge the fate of the pace of AI investments by hyperscalers," he said.
